title: Encrypted backup and fresh-store restore
description: Spec §10. scrypt-derived passphrase key, authenticated KDF header, bounded parameters, restore only into an empty store with a fresh vault key, bindings cleared and grants/approvals inactive.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T20: restore works with only the backup and passphrase; wrong passphrase, corruption, hostile KDF parameters and oversized backups fail safely
T21: restore uses a fresh key and leaves bindings absent and grants/approvals inactive pending review

plan: 2. Domain: the backup container (v1: scrypt N=131072, r=8, p=1, 32-byte salt, 32-byte key, AES-256-GCM with a fresh nonce; format and KDF parameters authenticated) with bounded sizes and parameters refused before any allocation; unit tests.

3. Application: runBackup and runRestore over a passphrase port and a backup-file port. Restore refuses any non-empty destination, generates a fresh vault key and id, preserves project records, and clears local bindings (approvals and grants do not exist in the state model yet; the obligation is recorded for WCLI-9/WCLI-12).

4. Adapters: hidden-input terminal passphrase reader (echo suppressed via raw mode, bounded, confirmation on create) and the backup file (created mode 0600 with O_EXCL and no overwrite, read bounded).
5. CLI and contract: ward backup --output <path>, ward restore --input <path>, manifest entries, error catalog additions, contract tests.

6. Tests: T20 six ways (round-trip with only the backup and passphrase; wrong passphrase; corruption; hostile KDF parameters; oversized backup; missing terminal) and T21 (fresh key and id, bindings absent), each measured against the pre-change state where applicable.
7. ADR 0006 recording the container format and the restore authority rules; docs sync and lore check --strict exit 0.
8. bun run check green, independent review dispatched over the diff, findings fixed, criteria checked on the branch, PR merged, dev promoted to main.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW RETURNED (2026-09-28, opum-workflow:reviewer over b1f4cb7..65ced49, dispatched after the handoff note). VERDICT: no high or medium finding. Crypto construction, validation ordering, restore authority and steady-state containment are sound; several protections were mutation-verified (a preserved-bindings mutant reddened exactly the two binding tests; dropping the revision from the AAD reddened the header-change case; file-chosen parameters reddened two). NINE LOW OR INFORMATIONAL FINDINGS, ALL DISPOSED: F1 the container recorded the header revision, which a concurrent writer can advance between the two reads — fixed by recording the plaintext own revision; F2 the early empty-destination guard was load-bearing and unpinnable (deleting it left every test green because store.create refuses with the same code and the key assertion read only the first item) — now pinned by asserting no passphrase was read and no item created, and the reviewer M5 mutant reddens it; F4 a directory was refused as "a file already exists" — the message now names both shapes; F5 the read path reused the create-flavoured message — reads now have backup_file_unreadable; F6 the backup file did not get the inherited-ACL strip the vault store applies — now shared through adapters/inherited-acl.ts; F7 the oversized test could not see the adapter own bound (the domain applies the same limit) — now pinned directly, and the reviewer M2 mutant reddens it; F8 the hostile-parameter test elapsed clause measured nothing (Node own maxmem refuses the huge set in 1 ms) — replaced by the canonical-N hostile-p case, which only the exact match stops; F9 a FIFO swapped in after the check would block forever — the read now opens O_NONBLOCK and the direct test bounds the elapsed time; hygiene: Ctrl-C now cancels rather than submitting what was typed (the catalog already described it as cancellation), the exported associated-data function is exercised by a test pinning every authenticated field, and an unused destructure is gone. F3 (a failed restore can leave a key nothing points at) is deliberately NOT changed in code — the key-before-vault order is what prevents the unrecoverable inverse — and is now recorded in ADR 0006 with its measured shape. WHAT THE REVIEW DID NOT CHECK, stated by it: the real terminal path (no pty), the packaged binary, the partial-write unlink path, two real concurrent processes, and CI itself. All fixes are in 523a124 on the branch; 347 tests / 0 fail; the three lore gates exit 0.

finalSummary: Landed on feat/WCLI-13-encrypted-backup-restore, PR opum-ai/ward-cli#32; the commit carrying the review fixes is 523a124, whose CI run 36501806822 is green (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity), and the closing commit is verified by its own run before the merge. WHAT: ward backup --output <path> seals the vault plaintext under a passphrase-derived key in a self-describing container - v1 is scrypt N=131072/r=8/p=1 with a fresh 32-byte salt and AES-256-GCM with a fresh nonce, with the domain, format version, origin vault id, revision and every KDF parameter authenticated as header data, so a relabelled container fails to open rather than being interpreted. A parameter set a file names is matched exactly and refused by name before any derivation allocates for it, which is also the CPU bound (a canonical N with a hostile p is refused, not derived). The passphrase is read only from a terminal with echo suppressed by raw mode and no mask printed, never from an argument, the environment or a pipe; Ctrl-C cancels the reading rather than submitting what was typed. The file is created once at mode 0600 with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, its inherited ACL stripped the way vault entries are, a failed write removes what it created, and reads are bounded, open non-blocking and refuse anything that is not a regular file. ward restore --input <path> refuses any non-empty destination before the terminal is consulted, before anything is read and before any key exists; it verifies and decodes the complete backup before committing state, mints a fresh vault id and key with the key stored before the vault (so an interrupted restore leaves at most a key nothing points at, never the unrecoverable inverse), keeps the project records and rebuilds the state with localBindings emptied, so a checkout registers again rather than inheriting authority. The fixed projection at the restore site is deliberately where WCLI-9 approvals and WCLI-12 grants will have to be dropped. ADR 0006 records the format, the authority rules, the orphan-key residue and the ACL strip. VERIFIED: criteria against tests as evidence, not code presence - T20 by test/backup.test.ts (round trip into a machine that shares nothing but the file and the passphrase, wrong passphrase, changed bytes in the ciphertext, the header and the parameter set, three hostile parameter sets, an oversized file, no terminal without a credential-store read, an existing file and a directory never replaced, a missing path, and directory/FIFO/link refused on the read path) and T21 by the same file (a key that differs from the original with the original vault and key untouched, project records preserved, localBindings empty, and the checkout registering again through the prompt). 347 tests / 0 fail; bun run check green; lore validate --strict, lore check --strict and lore agents --check exit 0. An independent opum-workflow:reviewer pass (spec section 15) returned no high or medium finding and nine low or informational ones, all applied in 523a124; its two unpinned-protection mutants were re-run here and now redden exactly the tests that name those protections - the early empty-destination guard (its removal left every test green because store.create refuses with the same code and the key assertion read only the first store item) and the adapter own read bound (masked by the domain applying the same limit) - and its other mutants already reddened the tests that name theirs. F3, a failed restore leaving a key nothing points at, is deliberately unchanged in code because the key-before-vault order prevents the unrecoverable inverse, and is recorded in ADR 0006 with its measured shape instead. NOT CHECKED, stated rather than implied: the real terminal path (no pty was driven; the byte reader is tested through a real descriptor but not a terminal), the packaged binary for these two commands, the partial-write unlink path, two real concurrent processes, and Linux/Windows.
